verifier_note: Checked against rtrb 0.4.0 (src/lib.rs, arc_ring_buffer.rs, README.md), assert_no_alloc 1.1.2 (src/lib.rs, README.md) and the current GlobalAlloc/std::alloc docs, all retrieved at the pinned versions; every check in this lane was also re-run myself through compile_oracle.py (rustc 1.98.1, jam set, host target) rather than taken on trust, plus one counter-example of my own. All four matched their prose: recipe 1 printed alloc_count=0, recipe 2's negative control printed alloc_count>0 (proving the counting allocator is sensitive, not vacuous), recipe 3 printed new_allocates ops_do_not with RingBuffer::new confirmed to allocate twice (Vec::with_capacity + Box::new, via arc_ring_buffer.rs) while push/pop touch only atomics and raw pointers, and recipe 4's own check printed sum=10, confirming the non-allocating branch. The lane's one systemic weakness is in recipe 4: unlike the zero-allocation claims (recipes 1 and 3), which are backed by an explicit negative control (recipe 2) proving the measurement apparatus actually detects an allocation, the 'aborts if the callback body allocates' half of recipe 4's claim ships with no check that ever allocates inside the closure -- the provided check only exercises the return-normally path. I closed that gap myself with a counter-example (Vec::push inside assert_no_alloc with AllocDisabler registered), which aborted exactly as documented (exit 0xC0000409, stderr 'memory allocation of 8 bytes failed'), so the underlying claim holds, but the recipe's own verification story was incomplete without it.
